results.result: H3 variants form heterotypic nucleosomes and do not preferentially associate with specific H2A variants. Mass spectrometry analysis revealed that ~60% of H3.1 and ~42% of H3.3 nucleosomes contain both H3 variants, and western blotting showed no preferential association between H3.1 or H3.3 and specific H2A variants.
results.evaluation: Claims C17-C18 provide quantitative MS data showing heterotypic H3 nucleosomes, while C19-C21 demonstrate through western blotting and MS that H3 variants do not preferentially associate with H2A variants. The data from Figure 1A-B directly support these conclusions with appropriate experimental evidence.

results.result: Most H3 modifications are not H3 variant-specific, with notable exceptions of H3K36 and H3K37 modifications preferentially associated with H3.3. Western blotting and mass spectrometry analyses showed that methylation and acetylation marks are present on both H3.1 and H3.3, though H3K36me and H3K37 modifications show enrichment on H3.3.
results.evaluation: Claims C22-C33 collectively demonstrate through western blotting (Figure 1C) and MS analysis (Figure 1D-E, supplements) that H3 modifications are largely variant-independent. The exception for H3K36/H3K37 is well-documented with quantitative data. The contrast with previous reports (C25) is appropriately noted.

results.result: H2A variants form homotypic nucleosomes with specific histone modification patterns. H2A.W associates with constitutive heterochromatin marks (H3K9me1/2, H3K27me1), H2A.Z with facultative heterochromatin marks (H3K27me3), and H2A/H2A.X with euchromatin marks (H3K36me3).
results.evaluation: Claims C36-C43 are supported by western blot data in Figure 1F showing distinct enrichment patterns of histone modifications with specific H2A variants. The co-precipitation data (C40-C41) demonstrates complex interplay between marks. This contrasts sharply with the H3 variant results, establishing H2A variants as key chromatin state determinants.

results.result: A 26-state ChromHMM model defines distinct chromatin domains in Arabidopsis. The model identifies constitutive heterochromatin (H1-6, 17% of genome), facultative heterochromatin (F1-6, 20%), euchromatin (E1-11), and intergenic regions (I1-3) based on histone modifications, variants, and genomic features.
results.evaluation: Claims C44-C51 describe the ChromHMM analysis with supporting data in Figure 2 and supplements. The 26-state model is justified as parsimonious (C44, Figure 2-supplement 2A), and each chromatin domain is characterized by distinct features (accessibility, methylation, transcription). The genome coverage percentages align with previous estimates (C47).

results.result: Chromatin states recapitulate H2A variant-histone modification associations observed in mononucleosomes. H2A.W and H3K9me1 define heterochromatic states, H2A.Z with H2AK121ub and H3K27me3 mark facultative heterochromatin, and H2A/H2A.X with H2Bub and H3K36me3 mark euchromatin.
results.evaluation: Claims C52-C56 demonstrate consistency between genome-wide chromatin states (Figure 2A) and mononucleosome biochemistry (Figure 1F). The emission probabilities in the ChromHMM model directly reflect the preferential associations observed in immunoprecipitation experiments, validating both approaches.

results.result: H2A variants are the most important histone variants for defining chromatin states. Sub-epigenome modeling showed that removing H2A variants caused loss of several states (Jaccard index <0.7), while removing H2B variants had minimal effect. Removing all histone variants had stronger impact than removing all H3 modifications.
results.evaluation: Claims C58-C63 are supported by systematic sub-epigenome analysis (Figure 2F) comparing models with different components removed. The Jaccard index quantitatively demonstrates H2A variants' importance. The comparison with the 9-state model (C58) and the hierarchy of contributions (H2A > H3 > H2B) are well-documented.

results.result: Loss of DDM1 profoundly perturbs chromatin states, particularly in constitutive heterochromatin. Concatenated modeling of wild-type and ddm1 showed that constitutive heterochromatin is replaced by facultative heterochromatin and intergenic states, while facultative heterochromatin and euchromatin states remain relatively stable.
results.evaluation: Claims C66-C71 are supported by concatenated ChromHMM analysis (Figure 3, Figure 3-supplement 1). The tissue/developmental stage comparison (C66) validates the approach, while the ddm1 analysis shows specific disruption of heterochromatic states with quantified genomic overlaps and Jaccard indices.

results.result: DDM1 binds both H2A.W and H2A.Z through the same conserved binding sites. Pull-down assays showed His6-tagged DDM1 co-precipitates H2A.W and H2A.Z but not H2A or H2A.X, with binding sites mapped to residues 100-123 and 639-673. The C-terminal tail of H2A.W is dispensable for binding.
results.evaluation: Claims C73-C77 are supported by systematic pull-down assays (Figure 3G-H, Figure 3-supplement 2). The experiments test full-length and truncated DDM1 fragments against different H2A variants, clearly demonstrating specific binding to H2A.W and H2A.Z through conserved regions. The deletion analysis (C75) provides additional mechanistic insight.

results.result: DDM1 prevents replacement of H2A.W by H2A.Z at TE genes in a transcription-independent manner. ChIP-seq analysis showed H2A.Z enrichment over TE genes in ddm1, including non-transcribed TEs, supporting that the H2A variant exchange is not governed by transcription.
results.evaluation: Claims C82-C85, C92 are supported by ChIP-seq data (Figure 4A) showing H2A.Z accumulation on both transcribed and non-transcribed TEs in ddm1. The key observation that non-transcribed TEs also accumulate H2A.Z (C84) directly supports the transcription-independent mechanism (C85, C92).

results.result: Transcription of TEs in ddm1 leads to acquisition of euchromatic chromatin states. Transcribed TEs show H2A.Z at TSS and H2A.X on gene bodies, with increased H3K36me3 enrichment correlating with transcription levels. Strongly expressed TEs accumulate euchromatic states while non-expressed TEs acquire facultative heterochromatin states.
results.evaluation: Claims C86-C91 are supported by ChIP-seq and chromatin state analysis (Figure 4A-C, Figure 4-supplement 1-2). The data show clear correlation between TE transcription levels and chromatin state transitions, with appropriate quantification of histone modifications and state assignments across expression quartiles.

results.result: Histone variants and modifications combine to define chromatin states across developmental stages and cell types. The study demonstrates strongest associations between homotypic H2A variant nucleosomes and histone modifications, while H3 variants form heterotypic nucleosomes with weaker modification associations.
results.evaluation: Claims C95-C101 represent the main conclusions synthesizing results from chromatin state modeling, biochemical analyses, and developmental comparisons. These are well-supported by the comprehensive dataset including ChromHMM models (Figure 2), mononucleosome analysis (Figure 1), and concatenated models (Figure 3-supplement 1A).

results.result: High H3K27me1 levels on H3.3 may result from demethylation of H3K27me3 or intermediate methylation states, and H3K36/H3K37 preference for H3.3 may relate to position 41 substitutions distinguishing H3.1 from H3.3.
results.evaluation: Claims C27 and C34 are speculative interpretations ('likely product', 'might be related') of observed data. While the observations of H3K27me1 on H3.3 and H3K36/37 enrichment are supported by data, the mechanistic explanations are hypotheses requiring additional experimental validation. The citations provide context but not direct evidence for these specific mechanisms.

results.result: The mechanism of H2A.W to H2A.Z replacement in ddm1 remains unclear. Two models are proposed: direct exchange by DDM1 (supported by convergent evolution with LSH) or indirect replacement due to loss of DNA methylation. Loss of H2A.W alone is unlikely to cause H2A.Z deposition.
results.evaluation: Claims C104-C108 present alternative mechanistic models that are speculative. While the observation of H2A.Z replacement is well-supported (C103), the mechanism is not definitively established. The evidence from H2A.W mutants (C108) argues against one possibility, but neither model is directly tested. Additional experiments would be needed to distinguish between mechanisms.

results.result: H2A variants may control chromatin writer/eraser activity with different affinities and efficacies. Examples include H2A.Z tail inhibiting H2B ubiquitin ligase, H2A.Z as major substrate for PRC1-mediated H2AK121Ub, and PRC2 preference for H2A.Z arrays.
results.evaluation: Claims C112-C117 propose a general model based on specific examples supported by citations (Surface et al. 2016, Gómez-Zambrano et al. 2019, Wang et al. 2018) and the current study's chromatin state data. While the general model (C116-C117) is somewhat speculative, the specific examples are well-documented. The proposal represents a reasonable synthesis of existing evidence.

results.result: Chromatin state maintenance involves replication-dependent recycling of histones in dividing cells, with H3.1 sustaining H3K27me3 and H3K27me1 deposition. In non-dividing cells, these mechanisms become inactive, allowing chromatin state changes through H3.3 deposition and H2A.Z eviction by INO80.
results.evaluation: Claims C118-C124 synthesize literature on chromatin maintenance mechanisms with appropriate citations (Reverón-Gómez et al. 2018, Jiang and Berger 2017, Jacob et al. 2014, Flury et al. 2023, Zhao et al. 2023, Willige et al. 2023). The logic connecting replication-dependent and -independent mechanisms is sound, though some aspects (C122, C124) involve inference beyond direct citation.

results.result: Unknown mechanisms may link H2A and H3 variant deposition to orchestrate PTM deposition in distinct chromatin states. A relationship between H3.3 and H3K36me1/2 was observed, and H3.3-H2A.Z dynamics appear coordinated in Arabidopsis and mammals.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C131 propose speculative models about coordinated histone variant deposition. While C129 is supported by citations showing H3.3-H2A.Z coordination, C128 is speculative ('possible preference'), and C130-C131 explicitly acknowledge unknown mechanisms. These represent hypotheses for future investigation rather than established findings.

results.result: Background on chromatin structure, histone variants, and their roles in transcription and chromatin organization. This includes established knowledge about nucleosome composition, histone variant diversity, ChromHMM applications, and variant-specific associations with chromatin domains.
results.evaluation: Claims C1-C16 represent well-established background knowledge supported by appropriate citations to foundational and recent literature. These provide context for the study but are not novel findings. All claims are appropriately referenced to primary literature.

results.result: Background on DDM1 function and evolutionary context. DDM1 causes H2A.W.6 deposition to heterochromatin and binds H2A.W specifically. H2A.W evolved independently in plants from macroH2A in animals, though both associate with heterochromatin and their deposition depends on related remodelers (DDM1/LSH).
results.evaluation: Claims C64-C65, C72, C78-C81 provide background on DDM1 and evolutionary context, all supported by appropriate citations including the authors' previous work (Osakabe et al. 2021). These establish the foundation for the current study's investigation of DDM1's role in H2A variant dynamics.

results.result: H3.1 shows relative enrichment with constitutive heterochromatin modifications, consistent with H3.1 being the preferred substrate for H3K27me1 deposition by ATXR5/6.
results.evaluation: Claims C126-C127 confirm previous findings (Johnson et al. 2004, Jacob et al. 2014) with the current study's data. This represents validation of prior work rather than a novel finding, but provides important context for interpreting the H3 variant results.

results.result: Specialized cell types like gametes likely harbor specific chromatin states not reflected in this study of vegetative tissues.
results.evaluation: Claim C98 is a reasonable prediction based on knowledge of gamete-specific histone variants (cited: Borg et al. 2020, 2021), but represents speculation about unstudied cell types. This appropriately acknowledges limitations of the current study's scope.

results.result: The authors demonstrate that H3 variants form heterotypic nucleosomes, with ~60% of H3.1 and ~42% of H3.3 nucleosomes containing both H3.1 and H3.3 variants. They also show that H3 variants do not preferentially associate with specific H2A variants, contrasting with the homotypic nature of H2A variant nucleosomes.
results.evaluation: Multiple reviewers explicitly affirm these findings. Reviewer 1 states the manuscript provides 'convincing evidence' that 'Arabidopsis nucleosomes are homotypic for H2A variants and heterotypic for H3 variants' and that 'H3 variants are not associated with specific H2A variants.' These are identified as 'important findings that contrast with previous observations in animal systems.'

results.result: The authors characterize the distribution of histone modifications on H3.1 and H3.3 variants, finding that most H3 modifications are present on both variants with some preferential associations (H3K36me and H3K37me with H3.3, H3K27me1 with H3.1), but overall showing that the vast majority of H3 modifications are not H3 variant-specific.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly states the manuscript provides 'convincing evidence' that 'H3 variants show no such strong associations with specific PTMs' (in contrast to H2A variants). Reviewer 2 confirms the authors 'confirm the association between certain marks and variants' and describes the biochemical analysis as 'solid' (Reviewer 3).

results.result: The authors demonstrate that H2A variants form homotypic nucleosomes with marked enrichment of specific histone modifications: H2A.W associates with constitutive heterochromatin marks (H3K9me1/2, H3K27me1), H2A.Z with facultative heterochromatin marks (H3K27me3), and H2A/H2A.X with euchromatin marks (H3K36me3).
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly affirms the manuscript provides 'convincing evidence' that 'H2A variants are strongly associated with specific histone post-translational modifications (PTMs).' Reviewer 2 states the authors 'confirm the association between certain marks and variants, in particular for H2A.' Reviewer 3 notes 'there is a tight association between H2A variants and histone modifications.'

results.result: The authors develop a 26-state chromatin model using ChromHMM that integrates histone variants and modifications, demonstrating that H2A variants are as important as histone modifications in defining chromatin states. The model distinguishes constitutive heterochromatin (H1-6), facultative heterochromatin (F1-6), euchromatin (E1-11), and intergenic regions (I1-3).
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 states the authors 'performed comprehensive epigenomic profiling' to produce a chromatin state map, revealing that 'histone H2A variants are as important as histone PTMs in defining the various chromatin states, which is unexpected and of high significance.' Reviewer 3 confirms 'H2A variants are major factors that differentiate euchromatin, facultative heterochromatin, and constitutive heterochromatin.'

results.result: Through sub-epigenome modeling, the authors demonstrate that removing H2A variants has the strongest impact on chromatin state definition compared to H2B or H3 variants, and that removing all histone variants has a stronger impact than removing all H3 modifications.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 2 notes the study 'nicely illustrates that, in Arabidopsis, histone variants (and H2A variants in particular) display specificity in modifications and genomic locations.' The computational analysis supporting H2A variant importance is implicitly accepted as reviewers describe the overall findings as 'well done' (Reviewer 4) and 'solid' (Reviewer 3).

results.result: The authors show that loss of DDM1 causes profound perturbation of constitutive heterochromatin states, with TEs losing constitutive heterochromatin and gaining facultative heterochromatin or euchromatin states, while facultative heterochromatin and euchromatin states remain largely unaffected.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly states 'The authors show that in ddm1 mutants, normally heterochromatic transposable element (TE) genes lose H2A.W and gain H2A.Z, along with the facultative heterochromatin and euchromatin signatures.' Reviewer 2 confirms the authors 'nicely describe the loss of constitutive heterochromatin in the ddm1 mutant.' Reviewer 3 notes 'the mutation in DDM1...causes the mis-assembly of chromatin states in TE region.'

results.result: The authors demonstrate through pull-down assays that DDM1 binds both H2A.W and H2A.Z (but not H2A or H2A.X) using the same conserved binding sites (residues 100-123 and 639-673), and that the C-terminal tail of H2A.W is dispensable for binding.
results.evaluation: The biochemical binding data is implicitly accepted by reviewers. Reviewer 3 states 'the biochemical analysis part is solid,' and no reviewer raises concerns about these specific binding experiments. The findings support the broader conclusions about DDM1 function that reviewers explicitly endorse.

results.result: The authors show that in ddm1 mutants, TEs accumulate H2A.Z (replacing H2A.W) in a transcription-independent manner, as both non-transcribed and transcribed TEs show H2A.Z enrichment, demonstrating that DDM1 prevents H2A.Z deposition at TE genes.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 explicitly affirms 'The authors show that in ddm1 mutants, normally heterochromatic transposable element (TE) genes lose H2A.W and gain H2A.Z.' The transcription-independent nature of this replacement is part of the accepted findings, as reviewers do not question this interpretation and the overall ddm1 analysis is described as well-executed.

results.result: The authors demonstrate that transcribed TEs in ddm1 show enrichment of H2A.Z at TSS and H2A.X on gene bodies, with strongly expressed TEs acquiring euchromatic states and marks (H3K36me3), while non-expressed TEs acquire facultative heterochromatin states.
results.evaluation: Reviewer 1 states the authors show that ddm1 mutants have TEs that gain 'the facultative heterochromatin and euchromatin signatures associated with H2A.Z at silent and expressed genes, respectively.' This transcription-dependent chromatin state transition is part of the accepted findings about ddm1 effects.

results.result: The authors conclude that histone modifications and variants combine into chromatin states that subdivide the genome, with H2A variants playing a prominent role in organizing chromatin states through their association with histone modifications, while H3 variants show weaker associations.
results.evaluation: This overarching conclusion is explicitly endorsed by multiple reviewers. Reviewer 1 calls it 'unexpected and of high significance.' Reviewer 2 states the study 'encourages future work in epigenomics to consider histone variants with as much attention as histone modifications.' Reviewer 4 describes it as 'an interesting and well done study.'

results.result: The authors conclude that tissue type and developmental stage (seedlings vs. leaves) do not have dramatic effects on chromatin state definition in wild-type plants.
results.evaluation: This finding is implicitly accepted as reviewers do not question the concatenated model analysis or raise concerns about tissue-specific effects. The overall chromatin state model is endorsed by reviewers as representing the 'prevalent organization of chromatin' (implicit in reviewer acceptance).

results.result: The authors propose mechanistic models for how DDM1 might mediate H2A variant exchange, either through direct H2A.Z to H2A.W exchange (supported by convergent evolution with mammalian LSH) or through indirect mechanisms involving DNA methylation loss.
results.evaluation: These are explicitly speculative models ('could exchange,' 'might be') that reviewers implicitly accept as reasonable interpretations. No reviewer challenges these mechanistic proposals, and the overall study is described as 'well-written' (Reviewer 3) with results 'clearly presented,' suggesting the speculative discussion is appropriate.

results.result: The authors propose that H2A variants control the activity of chromatin writers and erasers, with specific examples including H2A.Z inhibiting H2B ubiquitination and serving as the preferred substrate for PRC1 and PRC2.
results.evaluation: This mechanistic interpretation is implicitly accepted by reviewers as part of the broader conclusions about H2A variant importance. Reviewer 2 notes the study 'encourages future work' to consider histone variants, suggesting the proposed mechanisms are viewed as valuable contributions to the field.

results.result: The authors discuss how replication-dependent maintenance mechanisms involving H3.1 and H2A variant recycling sustain chromatin states in dividing cells, while non-dividing cells provide opportunities for chromatin state changes through H3.3 deposition and H2A.Z dynamics.
results.evaluation: This discussion of maintenance mechanisms is implicitly accepted as part of the overall framework. Reviewers describe the work as providing important insights into 'how histone variants shape the Arabidopsis epigenome' (Reviewer 1), which encompasses these mechanistic discussions.

comparisons.comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C22-C33 regarding H3 modifications being largely variant-independent. Both evaluations find the evidence convincing and supported, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming the manuscript provides 'convincing evidence' for these findings.

Perfect agreement on claims C36-C43 regarding H2A variants being strongly associated with specific PTMs. Both evaluations find the evidence well-supported, with peer reviewers explicitly affirming 'convincing evidence' and noting the 'tight association between H2A variants and histone modifications.'

Perfect agreement on claims C73-C77 regarding DDM1 binding specificity to H2A.W and H2A.Z. Both evaluations support these findings, with peer reviewers describing the 'biochemical analysis part is solid.'

Perfect agreement on claims C82-C85, C92 regarding H2A.Z accumulation on TEs in ddm1 mutants through a transcription-independent mechanism. Both evaluations find the evidence supported and well-executed.

Agreement on claims C104-C108, but with different evaluation types. OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN due to their speculative nature, while peer reviewers implicitly accept them as SUPPORTED reasonable interpretations. Both acknowledge the mechanistic proposals are not definitively established.

Agreement on claims C112-C117 regarding general models of H2A variant function. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED with acknowledgment of some speculation, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as valuable contributions to the field framework.

Agreement on claims C118-C124 regarding chromatin maintenance mechanisms. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED despite some inferential aspects, while peer reviewers implicitly accept these as part of the overall mechanistic framework.

Strong agreement on claims C86-C91 regarding transcription-dependent chromatin state transitions in ddm1. Both evaluations find the evidence supported. Peer review also includes C94, which OpenEval does not explicitly address in this result.

Strong agreement on claims C95-C97, C99-C101 representing main conclusions about H2A variant importance. Both evaluations strongly support these findings, with peer reviewers calling them 'unexpected and of high significance.' Peer review also includes C111.

Strong agreement on claims C67-C71 regarding ddm1 mutant effects on TE chromatin states. Both evaluations find the evidence supported. OpenEval also addresses C66 (tissue/developmental comparison), which peer reviewers address separately in R11.

Strong agreement on claims C17-C18, C20-C21 regarding heterotypic H3 nucleosomes and lack of H3-H2A variant associations. Both evaluations find evidence convincing. OpenEval does not include C19 in this result, while peer review does.

Agreement on claims C59-C62 regarding H2A variant importance demonstrated through sub-epigenome analysis. Both evaluations support these findings. OpenEval also includes C58 and C63, which peer reviewers address in R4.

Partial agreement on ChromHMM analysis claims C44-C51. Both evaluations support the chromatin state modeling. Peer review R4 also includes claims C52-C56 and C58, C63, which OpenEval addresses in separate results (R5 and R6).

Agreement on claims C52-C56 regarding consistency between genome-wide chromatin states and mononucleosome biochemistry. Both evaluations support these findings. These claims are part of peer review R4's broader assessment of the chromatin state analysis.

Partial overlap on claim C66 regarding tissue/developmental stage comparison in concatenated ChromHMM analysis. Both evaluations support this finding. OpenEval R7 focuses on ddm1 analysis (C66-C71), while peer review R11 addresses C66 as validation of the prevalent chromatin organization.
